clue.text: In part vaccinate to upset characteristic of tonic muscle spasms

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the run of letters is turned upside down, so read from bottom to top
In part says only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a vaccination might upset a patient prone to muscle spasms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' picks CINATET from 'vaccinATE TO' and 'upset' turns it round; the wordplay comes first and the medical definition fills the rest of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanic is the adjective for tetanus or tetany, conditions marked by sustained tonic contractions of the muscles.

clue.text: An émigrée confused in outlandish assortment of people

indicators.note: confused means the letters of these two words are muddled into a new order

parts.note: spelt out plainly these give A N E M I G R E E; the accent does not count in crosswords

explanation.surface: A bewildered émigrée finds herself among a strange crowd of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a menagerie is a strange or varied collection of people, borrowed from a collection of wild animals.

clue.text: Show preference for distinctive taste with no trace of lemon

indicators.note: with no says a letter is taken away from the word for taste

parts.note: a distinctive taste is a flavour

indicators.note: a trace of a word here is just its first letter

parts.note: first letter L

explanation.surface: A cook describes a dish with a special taste but not a hint of lemon.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour someone is to treat them with partiality, preferring them over others.

clue.text: American piano tested and commended

parts.note: P is the musical notation for piano, softly
proved can mean tested, as in a proving ground

explanation.surface: An American-made piano has been tried out and recommended.
explanation.definitionFit: Something approved has been sanctioned or spoken of favourably, much as a commended thing is praised.

clue.text: Contrary to inclination, say, not in favour of malt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for doing something against one's natural tendency

definitions.text: say, not in favour of malt
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: opposed to the grain, malt being an example of one ('say')

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from woodworking, where cutting across the grain is awkward; the second reading takes it literally, malt being a processed grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Going against the grain means acting contrary to one's natural disposition or preference.

clue.text: Interval for recreation of quiet song rhythm

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
a lay is a song or ballad
time is musical metre or rhythm

explanation.surface: A break for recreation is filled with a soft song and its rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Playtime is the school break when children are let out to play.

clue.text: Lyric about classical theatre

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A lyrical piece is written about an ancient theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lyric is also a London theatre name, which nudges the solver toward modern stages.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece and Rome an odeon was a roofed building for musical performances, hence the cinema name.

clue.text: Carry out, removing four from administrative body

indicators.note: removing says letters are taken out of the word for the body

parts.note: the executive is the branch of government that administers
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A sacking where four members are carried out of an administrative board.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute a plan or order is to perform or accomplish it.

clue.text: Regularly bone-idle male with advanced dropsy

indicators.note: Regularly means taking every other letter of the hyphenated word, here the even ones

parts.note: its second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A lazy man is suffering from an advanced case of dropsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is the old name for a build-up of fluid in body tissues, now called oedema (US edema).

clue.text: Came alive, impressed about adult range of knowledge

indicators.note: about means the word for impressed goes around the other pieces

parts.note: awed means deeply impressed
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
ken is one's range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: Someone became alert, struck by an adult's breadth of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Awakened means roused from sleep or stirred into activity, so brought to life.

clue.text: Marocain transformed into fanciful and extravagant thing

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of the fabric's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of marocain, a ribbed dress fabric, is made into an extravagant creation.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides pasta, macaroni once meant an affected dandy or anything showy and absurd, a Chambers sense.

clue.text: Discourse centred at heart on old Shetland viol

indicators.note: at heart picks the single middle letter of the seven-letter word

parts.note: middle letter T
a gue was a crude violin once played in Shetland, a dictionary word

explanation.surface: A lecture focuses on an ancient fiddle from the Shetland Isles.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue can mean speech or language, as in the gift of tongues, which is discourse.

clue.text: Son misguidedly admires Pops?

definitions.note: pops are guns, informally, and the question mark flags the slangy sense; plural like the answer

indicators.note: misguidedly means the letters of the word are scattered wrongly into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy wrongly hero-worships his father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pops' looks like fathers, but here it is slang for guns, pistols that go pop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidearms are handguns carried at the side, and a pistol can be called a pop or popgun.

clue.text: Two disheartened partners consuming round red fruit

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the central letter of the word

parts.note: the middle letter W is removed

indicators.note: consuming means the partners swallow up the round letter

parts.note: mates are partners
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Two downcast lovers eat a round red fruit together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomatoes are botanically fruits, typically red when ripe.

clue.text: Select refined and occasionally complex instrument

indicators.note: refined means the letters are worked over into a new order
occasionally takes every other letter of the word, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: its second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A buyer chooses a sophisticated and intricate device.
explanation.definitionFit: A telescope is an optical instrument for viewing distant objects.

clue.text: Ruling supporting power is full of meaning

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the word for ruling sits below the letter for power

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
regnant means reigning or ruling

explanation.surface: A court ruling backing state power is weighty with significance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant pause or remark is loaded with significance, carrying more than it says.

clue.text: Look into hospital careers, but not orderly

indicators.note: not orderly means the letters are out of order, rearranged

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Investigate jobs in hospitals, except for that of hospital orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly' looks like the hospital job; with 'not' it signals that the letters are out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: To research something is to investigate or study it closely.

clue.text: Throw into confusion energy estimates, essentially, over British fuel

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: essentially picks the central letter, the essence, of the nine-letter word

parts.note: middle letter M
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Energy forecasts about British fuel cause chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil is to involve in conflict or entangle, throwing affairs into disorder.

clue.text: Defeated second team gutlessly expelled

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers

indicators.note: gutlessly means the word has its insides removed, leaving just the outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters E and D

explanation.surface: A beaten reserve team is cravenly thrown out of the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwed is slang for beaten or cheated, left in a hopeless position.

clue.text: English team replacing head of operation in urgent situation

indicators.note: replacing head of means the first letter of the word is swapped out for the new pieces

parts.note: agency means operation or action, as in by the agency of
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: England's side takes over the running of an operation in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: An exigency is a pressing need or emergency demanding prompt action.

clue.text: Annoyance among committee of adjudicators

parts.note: in can mean among, as in one in a crowd
a jury is a panel that judges, as at a competition

explanation.surface: Irritation spreads within a judging panel.
explanation.definitionFit: Injury in an older sense is a wrong or offence done to someone, a grievance or affront.

clue.text: Be set back by old crooner in decline

indicators.note: set back means the little word is turned to run backwards

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the famous crooner of the mid-20th century

explanation.surface: Someone is left behind by an old singer whose career is fading.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbing, like a falling tide, means receding or waning.

clue.text: Some ad-libs enraged author

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An actor's improvised lines infuriated the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Republican thrown out and dismissed as inadequate

parts.note: ejected means thrown out

explanation.surface: A Republican politician is expelled and written off as not good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Rejected means refused or turned down as not acceptable.

clue.text: Country bird hiding in wrecked boat

indicators.note: hiding in means the bird sits concealed inside the other letters
wrecked means the letters of the vessel are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a swan is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird is sheltering inside a shipwreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked nation in southern Africa.

clue.text: Lacking grand kept firm hold on rent

indicators.note: Lacking says a letter is missing from the word for held

parts.note: gripped means held firmly
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Short of a thousand pounds, someone clings on to their rent money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid for housing; here it is the past participle of rend, torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent as the past form of rend means torn apart, the same as ripped.

clue.text: Microscopic organisms in great number on board

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the great number comes after the board

parts.note: a plank is a board
a ton, or tons, is a great number, informally

explanation.surface: Huge numbers of tiny creatures are found aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are the tiny plants and animals drifting in seas and lakes.
